preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 2 and 500 inclusive.
The number of roads m is between 0 and the maximum possible number of edges in a simple graph with n vertices.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v and 1 <= w <= 10**6 for u, v, w in edges)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities within the valid range and has a positive integer length up to 10^6.
The number of provided road descriptions matches m.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one integer for every distinct pair (s, t) with s < t.

postconditions.expression: all(c_st == 0 if dist(s, t) == float('inf') else len({e for e in edges if e in shortest_paths(s, t)}) for s, t, c_st in zip(pairs, output_values))
postconditions.description: For each pair (s, t) with s < t, the output value is 0 if no path exists, otherwise it is the count of unique edges that belong to at least one shortest path between s and t.

postconditions.expression: pairs == [(s, t) for s in range(1, n + 1) for t in range(s + 1, n + 1)]
postconditions.description: The output values correspond to pairs ordered lexicographically by s then t, specifically (1,2), (1,3)...(1,n), (2,3)...(n-1,n).
